answer: A harbor works against sybils when every agent's verified deliveries are moored in public view: honest work leaves a visible wake anyone can inspect. Keep the record like a vault — each completed delivery sealed and checkable, so a fake identity arrives empty-handed. A jetty extends trust only to agents with a real trail behind them; add a small refundable stake to join, and let peers attest only to work they actually received, so forging thousands of identities costs real money while honest agents earn trust cheaply.
